spark.scene: True-color view of the main Hawaiian Islands from northwestern islands to the large island in the southeast, with scattered white cumulus and elongated cloud bands over dark ocean and a thin gray veil over the ocean southwest of the central islands.

plumes.label: thin gray streak southwest of central islands
plumes.visual_description: thin translucent pale gray veil over dark ocean extending southwest from near the central islands, distinct from brighter white cumulus and cirrus

evidence: plume_id 1: thin gray streak SW of central islands, centroid 20.912,-158.187, length 236 km, area 10300 km2, land_frac 0.0, faint
upwind_end 21.26,-158.205 is 335.7 km from Mauna Loa and 367.8 km from Kilauea, not trailing from active vent

closest fire 18.7 km Honolulu n=21 far from summit (344.1 km) could be smoke source but size mismatch; other nearby clusters n=196 and n=86 at 333-335 km are within 5-22 km of Mauna Loa summit and are lava during eruption, not wildfire
volcanic_thermal_excluded 309 Mauna Loa + 91 Kilauea confirms active vents but summit region cloud-obscured in true-color
color thin pale gray favors aged vog over brown wildfire smoke or bright white cloud, but far-field transport not proven
per_plume.source_hint: far-field haze SW of Oahu/Molokai; Big Island vog source cloud-obscured vs small Honolulu fire

classify.caveats: Segmentation faint with low sam_confidence 0.45; Big Island source region is cloud-covered so continuity to vent cannot be verified; near-summit FIRMS clusters are lava from ongoing Mauna Loa NE rift eruption, not wildfires; light winds 6-17 kmh limit transport inference.

plumes.label: thin gray streak southwest of central islands

kilauea.activity_summary: The summit eruption of Kīlauea Volcano, within Halemaʻumaʻu crater, continued over the past 24 hours. All recent eruptive activity has been confined to the crater. No significant changes have been observed at the summit or in either rift zone.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: The Northeast Rift Zone eruption of Mauna Loa continues, with two active fissures feeding lava flows downslope. Fissure 3 remains the dominant source of the largest lava flow. The fissure 3 lava flows are traveling to the north toward the Daniel K.
